title: Candidate carries an attainable tier and a proof cost
description:
hire-attestors/src/claim.rs:65-74 -- Candidate carries source, domain, path, display_name and nothing else. Two facts the candidate list and the lazy-proof path both need are missing:

  attainable tier -- what this candidate COULD prove if asked. Distinct from
    Claim::assurance(), which exists only on the far side of prove(). This is
    the field that makes 'prove lazily in descending attainable tier' (the
    upgrade path named at hire-grpc/src/service.rs:288) expressible at all.

  proof cost -- silent, or requires a human touch. The epic's standing
    constraint is that FetchJWTSVID never prompts, and that constraint is
    unenforceable without this field.

Design care: attainable tier is a CLAIM ABOUT THE FUTURE made by the attestor, and Claim::derive deliberately takes no level so that a tier can never be asserted without evidence. Keep that property. The attainable tier must not be usable as an input to derive(), must never appear in an issued token, and must be typed so it cannot be confused with a proven assurance level -- a bare AssuranceLevel on Candidate would re-open exactly the hole the Candidate/Claim split was built to close (see README 'Until recently the type system let a cheap discovery call fabricate an attestation').
acceptance_criteria: Attainable tier is a distinct type from proven assurance; a compile-time or test-level demonstration that it cannot reach Claim::derive or an issued token.
